Reportedly, Apple achieved its first-ever annual sales in India surpassing US$10 billion in the previous fiscal year.

This achievement is particularly remarkable in a country where the average annual income is less than US$3,000—especially considering that iPhones are priced higher in India than in the U.S....

For many years, iPhone sales in India were negligible for Apple. But that has changed dramatically in recent years, and combined with local economic growth, Apple has finally been able to open Apple Stores locally.

Bloomberg reported this latest milestone today.

Given the local income levels and the fact that iPhones are actually manufactured in India, one might expect local prices to be far lower than in the U.S. In reality, however, due to high taxes, Apple products are priced higher in India than in the U.S.

Apple has attempted to offset this gap to some extent by partnering with banks to offer credit card rebates.

Currently, about a quarter of iPhones are made in India, but most are shipped back to the U.S. for sale. Apple has restructured its logistics arrangements to avoid U.S. tariffs on imports from China.
